regler.skal: JS may set data-state. It may not paint.
State names intent: lage, mark, open, laddad.
data-atgard is the wire. One table should own it.
data-* is the declarative state. CSS reads it.
Page scripts are closures. Nothing is written to window.
A unit does one job. Empty and unreferenced units are dead.
One state change should fan out by subscription, not by a list of calls.
Labels and indexes are derived from the source state.
Storage, history, and DOM writes have a named boundary.
data-las is the scroll lock. Motion time comes from --tau.
Script still carries raw numerals (0.369, 0.45, 36, lerp 0.1). They are not token quantities.
Enter, Space, and arrow keys are handled. prefers-reduced-motion is read. :focus-visible is in CSS.
The page script is one closure. Dev tools are not part of that API.
Scroll and resize go through rAF. They do not paint layout in a loop.
Home, archive, project, and info are the page kinds.
Color, type, space, and time come from tokens.
site.css declares @layer reset, tokens, falt, komponenter, dev.
A component that must travel uses a container query.
Block classes scope component rules.
Rules key off data-state, not a class thrown from JS.
There is no utility-class stack.
html[data-satt] reassigns --rad-* and the halo. No per-component theme file.
Breakpoints change --u and --cols. Chrome may be fixed to the viewport.
Motion uses --tau. Reduced motion zeroes it. Layout props stay still.
The reset star is the only universal selector that should exist.
:focus-visible uses the stroke token.
Type and the row step steer the hierarchy.
@supports guards the round() baseline snap. The plain --falt-rader remains when it is missing.
Logical properties keep the field in either writing direction.
Names stay on the block. One-off breakpoints and unlayered files are the leak.
